title: Protecting Your Accounts
blurb: Passwords, two-step login and safe habits.
cards: Long beats clever. A phrase of several random words is strong and easy to remember. Never reuse a password, because one leak then opens every account.
Length and randomness win. Four or more random words is hard to crack.
Using the same password everywhere is fine if it is strong.
If one site leaks it, attackers try it everywhere. Use a different one for each account.
Two-step verification asks for a code or approval on your phone as well as your password. Even if someone steals your password, they still cannot get in.
What does two-step login protect against?
Someone getting in with only a stolen password
A stolen password is not enough without the second step.
You are on public Wi-Fi. What should you avoid?
Logging in to your bank without extra protection
Use mobile data for banking when you can, since public networks are easier to snoop on.
example: You get a text saying your bank account is locked. Open the bank app you already use instead of tapping the message link, and check alerts there.
